newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, no impact from M3 data.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, no impact from M3 data.

text.p: Dutch money rates were glued to previous levels on Monday and dealers said trade was slow as the demand for liquidity had eased since the Dutch central bank set a new credit quota last week. The German M3 figure was ignored.
German M3 for September had no impact as the slowdown to 8.4 percent versus the 8.7 percent in August was in line with expectations, dealers said.

Last week call money rates were high, as some players were short of liquidity near the expiry of the three-month credit quota and the special advances pact did not offer sufficient liquidity to solve the shortage for some market players.
The credit quota sets a limit for commercial banks' borrowing from the central bank at the secured loans rate, which is currently set at 2.00 percent.
The special advances, short-term loans offered to commercial banks, is currently pegged at 2.50 percent and the central bank allocated 2.46 billion guilders under the latest scheme.
Call money was traded at 2.75 percent bid, unchanged from last Friday, when the market had already reacted to the new credit quota. A few days earlier call money traded above 3.00 percent bid.
Dealers noted some trade in Dutch Treasury Certificates.
"But trade is not wild," said one dealer, adding prices were reasonable at 2.84 percent for January DTCs, 2.85 for February and 2.86 for March.
The guilder was steady at 112.17 per 100 marks versus 112.175 on Friday.
